recommendation: Reject expanding merchant operational_owner. Canonical-document write is the safer lower-cost candidate, but do not implement/approve PR-B yet: it did not establish absence of material interactive regression.
why: Canonical fixes the controlled snapshot race without requiring all writers to cooperate; owner greatly magnifies conflicts/CPU/sync delay. Canonical still raises physical hot-order p95 by 11.6%,22.4%,15.8% across paired trials and has 65 interactive errors vs49 baseline in 100-order same-merchant overload.
limits: Instrumented in-process ASGI, not public-network or production SLO measurements.
Sync load represents actual modifying persistence segments; unchanged-status worker early exits and external Salla HTTP are not modeled.
Virtual fixture is an operational note without material demand; physical fixture uses real stock.
Single-node replica set does not test failover.
Three finite-burst trials are not a sustained seasonal capacity proof.
Mongo I/O unavailable due process permissions; client CPU/I/O and Mongo CPU retained.
p95/p99 near90seconds are deadline-censored; ratios close to1 do not establish equivalence.
No fixed materiality margin was assumed; reported actual changes prevent claiming blanket no-regression.

comparison.percentile_method: Each cell reports median of the three independently measured trial percentiles, not a pooled request percentile. Raw requests remain in Actions artifacts.
comparison.performance_gate: No assumed materiality threshold; all request errors and deadline failures retained.
